chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadda', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The quickest of the rewards for a good deed is for maintaining good relationships with the relatives'.

key_terms.صِلَةُ الرَّحِمِ: Maintaining kinship ties / Good relations with relatives

ai.seo_question: What is the fastest way to receive reward for good deeds according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise yet profound statement from Imam al-Sadiq (as) attributing to the Prophet (saww) that maintaining kinship ties (*silat al-rahim*) yields the swiftest reward. This emphasis on immediacy distinguishes it from other virtues, underscoring its critical role in preserving social cohesion and divine favor within the Shia ethical framework. The hadith serves as a foundational text for the jurisprudential and spiritual obligations of family relations.
